input.reasoning_summary:
The claim that Coca-Cola's Bottling Investments segment is "a drag on overall profitability" in 2025 is SUPPORTED by the evidence. 

Evidence E9 shows that for the year ended December 31, 2025, Bottling Investments had an operating margin of only 7.4%, which is:
- 21.3 percentage points below the consolidated margin of 28.7%
- 32.3 percentage points below EMEA (39.7%)
- 51.7 percentage points below Latin America (59.1%)
- 18.5 percentage points below North America (25.9%)
- 30.9 percentage points below Asia Pacific (38.3%)

Evidence E4 shows that Bottling Investments contributed only 3.1% of total operating income in 2025, the smallest positive contribution among all operating segments, despite presumably representing a meaningful portion of revenues (as E2 notes that finished product operations generate higher revenues).

A segment operating at 7.4% margin when the consolidated company achieves 28.7% margin mathematically drags down overall profitability - the consolidated margin would be higher if the Bottling Investments segment performed at the level of other segments. This establishes that the segment is indeed "a drag" on overall profitability in the sense that it dilutes the company's consolidated profitability metrics.
